title: Bind provider-owned reasoning, fallback, billing, and transcript loss to canonical UNIIMENTE attempts
problem: Official provider changes from 2026-09-23 through 2026-09-29 introduce a new Claude Sonnet contract, account-bound reasoning artifacts that may be silently dropped, billed no-output refusals and multi-attempt fallback accounting, reduced Compliance API metadata, an incident that may have left Claude messages unsaved, an OpenAI image-encoder correction, and a Kimi file-service incident. UNIIMENTE must preserve one authority, event, attempt, evidence, cost, and runtime plane while its current Kernel history now proves direct Claude-assisted collaboration.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20260901-provider-change weekly provider-change intake on draft PR 105
INTENT-0030 preserve the effect; do not literalize the metaphor
baseline: Draft PR 105 already treats provider sessions, compaction, permissions, search, dynamic tools, diagnostics, billing corrections, and compliance transcripts as subordinate leased evidence. Current main is 25ab9b4b; its latest merged hotfix records Claude Opus 5.5 as a coding contributor and links a Claude session, but the four default branches contain no Anthropic or Kimi runtime adapter. DALEOBANKS alone has a direct provider API path, using OpenAI gpt-4o-mini Chat Completions and optional text-embedding-3-small.

alternatives.name: Narrow draft update
alternatives.description: Add a dated evidence packet and only the new invariants for provider-artifact account binding, per-attempt refusal/fallback accounting, and provider-transcript loss; keep PR 105 draft.
advantages: Closes silent semantic-loss and cost-ledger gaps
disadvantages: Adds more policy text to an undecided draft
Requires future adapter fixtures to prove behavior
alternatives.revival_evidence: Selected because current main contains direct Claude-assisted collaboration and official changes create genuinely new replay, cost, and persistence invariants.

alternatives.name: Brief only
alternatives.description: Report the changes without repository mutation.
disadvantages: Leaves account-bound artifact drops and billed no-output attempts implicit
Does not durably bind today's transcript-loss evidence to the protocol
alternatives.revival_evidence: Use for the next cycle with no new invariant, deadline, or direct exposure, or if the founder chooses brief-only reporting.

alternatives.name: Immediate provider migration
alternatives.description: Adopt Claude Sonnet 5.5, provider fallback, or another new provider feature now.
disadvantages: No approved adapter or independent eval
Can duplicate retries, costs, sessions, and authority
Would require credentials and routing authority
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder approval plus deterministic fixtures, independent evaluation, data and residency review, cost ceiling, receipt mapping, and a sandbox canary.

alternatives.name: Provider-native orchestration
alternatives.description: Let provider sessions, fallback, transcripts, and usage records become the workflow and cost source of truth.
disadvantages: Provider artifacts can be silently dropped or unsaved
Provider usage summaries can hide individual attempts
alternatives.revival_evidence: Do not revive unless it can be proven to remain a replaceable adapter inside the existing canonical runtime with complete attempt and effect receipts.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: The current runtime continues unchanged and no immediate production failure is expected because no affected model or endpoint is configured on the four default branches.
disadvantages: Direct Claude-assisted work can lose provider-only reasoning or transcript state without a durable warning
Future fallback integrations may undercount billed attempts or treat silent artifact drops as equivalent replay

roles.position: Preserve broad multi-model collaboration, including Claude-assisted coding, while keeping model sessions and reasoning artifacts subordinate to founder intent and canonical repository evidence.
material_concerns: Model migration becoming de facto authority
Provider transcript treated as institutional memory

roles.position: Bind every provider artifact and fallback iteration to one canonical attempt graph; a successful response after a dropped block is not replay-equivalent.
evidence_refs: Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 release and preserved-thinking docs

roles.position: Assume HTTP 200, empty output, provider recovery, and a visible session can all mislead: billing, execution, or data loss may still have occurred.
Require model-account-conversation fingerprints, input-transformation logs, usage.iterations, serving-model receipts, and recovery canaries before any provider feature is promoted.
Treat organization-bound reasoning, Compliance IDs, and provider transcripts as sensitive scoped artifacts; never widen access merely to make incomplete activity records convenient.

evidence.claim: Claude Sonnet 5.5 launched on 2026-09-28 with five breaking contract changes and $2/$10 per MTok pricing.
evidence.finding: Thinking settings, forced tool choice, preserved thinking, computer-use types, advisor pairings, and progress-output shape differ from Sonnet 5.

evidence.claim: Sonnet 5.5 thinking blocks are model-, conversation-, and account-bound and may be silently dropped while a request still succeeds.
evidence.finding: The beta header exposes model_binding_mismatch, prefix_binding_mismatch, and organization_binding_mismatch in input_transformations; without it some drops are silent.

evidence.claim: From 2026-09-24, some Claude refusals before output are billed and fallback can create multiple separately billed attempts.
evidence.finding: bio, frontier_llm, and reasoning_extraction pre-output refusals are billed; usage.iterations is the per-attempt accounting record and top-level usage covers only the serving attempt.

evidence.claim: Anthropic's 2026-09-29 incident affected Claude API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork, and some messages between 14:00 and 14:59 UTC may not have been saved.
evidence.finding: Provider recovery does not prove provider-side conversation completeness or task non-execution.

evidence.claim: Current Kernel main directly records Claude-assisted collaboration but no Anthropic runtime adapter exists on any inspected default branch.
evidence.reference: GitHub connector inspection at Kernel 25ab9b4b, DALEOBANKS e2f1ebed, WMI ec82b802, and PumpStation db6758df
evidence.finding: Kernel commit 25ab9b4b names Claude Opus 5.5 and a Claude session; code search found only agent-entry and historical collaboration records, not an Anthropic client or runtime route.

counterevidence.claim: The releases require an immediate production model migration.
counterevidence.reference: Default-branch code search and exact adapter paths observed 2026-09-29
counterevidence.finding: DALEOBANKS remains on gpt-4o-mini and text-embedding-3-small; no gpt-6, Sora, Anthropic API, or Kimi API runtime token was found.

counterevidence.claim: Every weekly incident requires another protocol rule.
counterevidence.finding: OpenAI's corrected image encoder and Kimi's resolved file-service incident are adequately covered by current canary, retry, and receipt rules absent direct exposure.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Keep Claude, OpenAI, Kimi, and future provider capabilities replaceable and useful while one canonical attempt, evidence, cost, authority, and runtime plane remains replay-safe through provider artifact loss, silent transformation, fallback, and outage.

advantages.statement: Account- and model-bound artifact fingerprints make semantic replay loss observable.
advantages.amplified_value: Cross-provider and cross-account handoffs become explicit migrations instead of silent degradation.

advantages.statement: Per-attempt billing and fallback records make cost and retry behavior auditable.
advantages.amplified_value: The same ledger can prevent duplicate effects, expose provider cost drift, and support independent optimization.

disadvantages.statement: Capturing organization identity for reasoning artifacts can expose sensitive account topology.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Store an opaque provider-account binding identifier or policy-permitted hash, never credentials or secret material, with least-privilege access.

disadvantages.statement: A successful response after a dropped artifact can be misclassified as successful replay.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Treat input_transformations or missing bound artifacts as a new semantic attempt requiring explicit migration status and independent evaluation.

disadvantages.statement: Fallback can issue multiple attempts, incur multiple charges, and obscure the model that actually answered.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Preserve usage.iterations, model IDs, stop categories, fallback boundaries, and credits under one canonical idempotency identity; never infer cost from top-level usage alone.

disadvantages.statement: Provider transcript loss can erase collaboration evidence or invite duplicate work.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Make repository commits, canonical events, and receipts the durable record; a missing provider transcript is ambiguous, never proof that work or an effect did not occur.

disadvantages.statement: New model migration fixtures could become a second provider-specific harness or scheduler.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Run fixtures only in the existing test substrate with no daemon, queue, credentials, live route, or independent retry loop.

disadvantages.statement: Another model-authored protocol update can normalize policy accumulation while PR 105 remains undecided.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Limit this update to three new invariants supported by direct Claude collaboration evidence; keep the PR draft and regress to brief-only on the next immaterial cycle.

comparisons.baseline: Existing draft covers provider sessions, raw artifacts, dynamic tools, incidents, and append-only billing adjustments, but not account-bound artifact drops, per-attempt refusal billing, or provider transcript non-persistence.
comparisons.do_nothing: No runtime regression is expected today, but collaboration provenance and future cost accounting remain vulnerable to silent provider behavior.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: A brief-only warning reduces process but does not produce a durable testable contract for newly direct Claude-assisted collaboration.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Provider-native sessions and fallback own replay and cost, reducing adapter work but violating canonical ownership and no-duplicate-runtime constraints.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Deterministic offline fixtures can represent dropped blocks, usage iterations, refusal categories, unsaved transcript state, and serving-model changes without a live account.

rejected_alternatives.name: Switch collaboration to Sonnet 5.5 immediately
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: No independent evaluation, account-binding fixture, or founder routing decision exists.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder-approved sandbox comparison with complete replay, provenance, cost, and rollback evidence.

rejected_alternatives.name: Inspect provider accounts and billing
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The scheduled reviewer has no authority to inspect credentials, contracts, balances, invoices, or account linkages.

rejected_alternatives.name: Build a provider failover daemon
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: It would create a second scheduler/runtime and could duplicate effects.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: None unless implemented inside the canonical runtime under founder approval and proven receipt-safe.

pass_2.attack_summary: The Pass-1 safeguards can still leak account structure, overfit to Anthropic field names, turn missing transcripts into automatic retries, let cost evidence authorize routing, or let weekly documentation become de facto policy.

new_weaknesses.statement: Hard-coding input_transformations or usage.iterations would overfit the canonical contract to one provider.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Map provider fields into generic subordinate artifact-transformation and attempt-accounting events while preserving raw provider payloads.

new_weaknesses.statement: A missing transcript flag could trigger duplicate replay instead of escalation.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Classify missing provider history as ambiguous and require canonical receipt checks; never auto-retry consequence-bearing work.

new_weaknesses.statement: Opaque account hashes can become an unauthorized identity authority.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Use them only as compatibility metadata; canonical passports, grants, and legal principals remain authoritative.

new_weaknesses.statement: A reviewer can label every vendor detail a new invariant to keep editing the protocol.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require direct exposure or a previously uncovered authority, replay, cost, privacy, or runtime failure mode; otherwise publish no repository change.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Only opaque compatibility metadata is retained; secrets and raw credential material remain prohibited.
Dropped artifacts create an explicit semantic-migration state, not replay equivalence.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any provider input transformation or artifact rejection

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Each provider iteration is a subordinate attempt with distinct model, cost, refusal, and credit data under one canonical identity.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any provider fallback or refusal integration

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Provider transcript presence or absence is non-authoritative; canonical commits, events, and receipts govern recovery.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any provider incident reporting unsaved or missing messages

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: No standalone migration harness, daemon, queue, session owner, or retry loop may be created.
This cycle has direct Claude collaboration exposure and three new contract gaps; the PR remains draft with explicit founder decision and next-immaterial-cycle regression criteria.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Founder review of PR 105 or the next weekly cycle

pass_2.final_design: Update draft PR 105 only: add the 2026-09-29 evidence and validated deliberation; extend section 7 with generic rules for account/model/conversation-bound artifacts, per-attempt refusal and fallback accounting, and provider transcript loss. Make no runtime, route, model, credential, account, billing, authority, or production change.

residual_risks.risk: Live provider account linking, contracts, residency, invoices, and deployment configuration remain unknown.
residual_risks.mitigation: Require separate authorized-human inventory before any adoption or billing conclusion.

residual_risks.risk: The same agent produced all five perspectives.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep PR 105 draft and require founder or independent human review before merge or adoption.

residual_risks.risk: Official documentation and billed refusal categories can change in place.
residual_risks.mitigation: Preserve observation date, official URLs, exact model and field names, and future deterministic fixtures.

dissent.handling: Preserve the objection in the review and PR. The docs-only update may proceed because the current default branch proves direct Claude-assisted collaboration and official changes add unhandled replay, cost, and persistence failure modes. Merge and adoption remain founder decisions.

entries.position: Stop recurring model-authored protocol accumulation while PR 105 remains undecided.
entries.rationale: Accurate weekly additions still create review debt and can become de facto policy without founder ratification.
entries.evidence_threshold: After this update, make no repository change unless a new direct exposure, hard deadline, or previously uncovered canonicality, authority, retry, cost, privacy, or no-duplicate-runtime invariant appears.
entries.review_trigger: Founder review of PR 105 or the next weekly cycle

migration_plan: No runtime migration. If Sonnet 5.5, provider fallback, or another affected feature is proposed, first add generic adapter events and deterministic fixtures for account/model/conversation binding, input transformations, refusal categories, usage iterations, serving-model changes, transcript loss, and receipt-gated recovery. Only a separately authorized sandbox canary with independent evaluation, data/residency review, cost ceiling, and rollback may precede production consideration.

steps: Leave draft PR 105 unmerged or revert the 2026-09-29 documentation-only commits
Preserve the dated evidence and dissent as historical records
Regress recurring repository updates to brief-only reporting if the materiality gate is not met

kill_criteria: Any write to a default branch or merge without founder approval
Any model, production, credential, account, invoice, contract, or routing change
Any provider-owned canonical workflow, event, identity, authority, memory, evidence, receipt, evaluator, or cost ledger
Any retry of consequence-bearing work based only on missing provider transcript state
Any silent acceptance of a dropped account-, model-, prefix-, or conversation-bound provider artifact as equivalent replay
Any collapse of provider fallback iterations into one cost or attempt record
Any second scheduler, durable provider session owner, retry daemon, or agent runtime
Any credential or raw account-binding secret stored in compatibility evidence
Any same-provider sole evaluation of promotion or evidence quality
Any unauthorized Compliance API or transcript lookup
Any ineligible retention or residency path
review_trigger: Founder review of draft PR 105; any Sonnet 5.5, provider fallback, cross-account replay, Compliance API, gpt-6 image/computer-use, Kimi file/search, or provider-transcript recovery proposal; any future incident with missing provider messages or ambiguous completion
